list: Follow the rule of thirds: put eyes or the horizon on an imaginary line one third in from the edge.
Leave a little space in the direction a person is looking or moving.
Crop out distracting edges – bins, cables, half-visible people – rather than the subject.

sections: Cropping removes part of the picture and changes its shape; resizing keeps the whole picture and changes its pixel dimensions; *trimming* usually means removing plain borders automatically. To make a round profile picture use [Circle Crop Image](/circle-crop-image/); to split one image into pieces use [Image Splitter](/image-splitter/).

sections: The tool reads JPG, PNG, WebP, GIF, BMP, AVIF and – via built-in decoders – HEIC photos from iPhones, so you rarely need to convert first.

It runs in Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari on Windows, macOS, Linux, ChromeOS, Android and iPhone/iPad. On a phone, tap the drop area to pick from your gallery; results are saved to Downloads or the Files app. Batches are processed one after another and downloaded together as a ZIP, so a whole holiday album takes only a few taps.

Edits are made at the full resolution of the original. JPG and WebP results are encoded at high quality (about 90 %), which is visually identical to the original for most photos while keeping files compact; choose PNG when you need lossless output or transparency. To shrink files further afterwards use [Compress Image](/compress-image/), and to change dimensions use [Resize Image](/resize-image/).

list: **The file will not open** – check it is a real image and not a shortcut or a cloud placeholder; download it fully from iCloud, Google Photos or OneDrive first.
**The result looks blurry** – start from the original, not a thumbnail sent through WhatsApp or Messenger, which recompress photos heavily.
**Colours look slightly different** – wide-gamut (Display P3) photos are shown in sRGB, the standard for the web; this is normal and consistent across devices.
**The download does not appear on iPhone** – look in Files → Downloads, or long-press the preview and choose Save to Photos.
**A big batch is slow** – very large photos use a lot of memory; close other tabs or process 20–30 images at a time.

sections: Everything happens inside your browser tab. Your images are read from your disk into memory, processed there and saved straight back to your device. Nothing is uploaded, stored or logged, there is no account, and the tool keeps working offline once the page has loaded – so it is safe for private, confidential and unreleased material.
